name: REF35205QDBVR
title: REF35 nanopower precision series voltage reference, 1.024 V to 5.0 V
summary: The REF35 family are series band-gap references drawing 650 nA typical, with ±0.05 % initial accuracy and a drift limit of 12 ppm/°C (SOT-23, -40 °C to 105 °C) or 10 ppm/°C (WCSP, -40 °C to 85 °C). The output buffer sources 10 mA and sinks 5 mA; dropout is at most 250 mV at 10 mA and the input runs to 6 V. An EN pin shuts the part down to 0.1 µA max at 25 °C and an NR pin lets one capacitor filter the band-gap noise. Thirteen fixed voltages come in a 6-pin SOT-23 and eight in a 4-ball WCSP; REF35180QDBVR is the 1.8 V SOT-23.

circuits.title: Connection diagram
circuits.description: The reference powered from its input with EN tied to VIN, so it is always on. A 0.1 µF capacitor decouples the input and a 1 µF capacitor sits on the output. A capacitor from NR to ground is optional and carries no value.

circuits.title: Basic connections
circuits.description: AVDD feeds VIN and EN together. CIN bypasses the supply and CL sits from the REF output to ground; CL must have under 400 mΩ ESR for the output to stay stable. The NR capacitor is optional.

circuits.title: Positive and negative reference voltages with OPA735
circuits.description: A REF35250 on +5 V gives +2.5 V. The OPA735 is an inverting amplifier of gain -1 (R1 and R2 both 10 kΩ, non-inverting input grounded), so its output is -2.5 V; it runs from +5 V and -5 V. R1 and R2 need matched temperature coefficients.

circuits.title: Precision supply and reference for the ADS7038
circuits.description: A REF35500 on a +6 V input supplies 5 V to the AVDD pin of an ADS7038, which uses AVDD as its reference, so the ADC's 0 V to 5 V range is set by the REF35. 0.1 µF and 1 µF bypass the input; 10 µF and 0.1 µF sit on the output. A unity-gain op-amp buffer drives the ADC input through an RC filter. NR is open.
notes: Misprint: VIN (pin 4) should read connected to +6 V with EN (pin 3).

operation.text: The input may sit anywhere from VREF + VDO up to 6 V. Dropout is 250 mV at most with a 10 mA load, and at no load the part works with the supply only 50 mV above the output. Quiescent current is 650 nA typical and 2.6 µA at most over temperature. A 0.1 µF to 10 µF bypass capacitor on the supply is recommended.

EN high, or EN unconnected at power-up, puts the part in active mode; EN low shuts it down, the output goes high-impedance and supply current falls to 100 nA at room temperature. EN has no internal pull-up and draws no extra current when held low. An open-drain driver needs a pull-up resistor to VIN. EN must never be above VIN. When going from shutdown to active, EN must be driven, not floating. If EN is left unconnected, the parasitic capacitance on it must stay under 30 pF. Logic thresholds are 0.7 × VIN (high) and 0.3 × VIN (low).

NR reaches the band-gap through an internal 60 kΩ. A capacitor from NR to ground forms a low-pass filter with it: 1 µF puts the corner near 2.7 Hz, and more capacitance lowers it further and cuts output noise. The capacitor's leakage shifts accuracy and drift, so it should be a low-leakage type. An NR capacitor lengthens start-up. NR may be left open.

The class-AB output buffer sources 10 mA and sinks 5 mA with no dead zone around zero load. A capacitor of 0.1 µF to 10 µF is required from VREF to ground, with ESR below 400 mΩ. Low-ESR, low-inductance ceramic (X5R, X7R or similar) works best; an electrolytic output capacitor needs a 0.1 µF ceramic beside it. Extra output capacitance (10 µF in parallel) improves the response to load steps but slows start-up. At the input, 1 µF to 10 µF (ceramic or electrolytic) helps where the supply moves.

The output settles to its accuracy without ringing. Turn-on to 0.1 % is 2 ms typical with 1 µF and no load and scales with VREF; start-up time rises with the output voltage, the output capacitance and the NR capacitance.

Load current and input voltage set the dissipation; at high ambient temperature the allowed load current may be below the 10 mA sourcing capability, so TJ = TA + PD × RθJA must stay within the rating.

Reflow stresses the die and shifts the output. In a test of 32 units on one FR4 board (1.66 mm thick, 174 mm × 135 mm) through one lead-free reflow, every shift was under 0.03 %; larger, thicker or different boards may give more. Each further reflow adds shift, so on a two-sided board the reference goes on in the last pass.

Measured on ordinary FR4 boards with no stress-relief slots and no burn-in, held at 35 °C in an oil bath and read every 30 minutes. The SOT-23 drifts 40 ppm typical over the first 1000 hours and 55 ppm over 2000 hours; most of the drift comes in the first 1000 hours. The figure is typical, not guaranteed.
Measured with the part soldered to a board baked at 150 °C for 30 minutes first: the change in the 25 °C output after a cycle through the temperature range and back.

Low-frequency (1/f) noise grows with output voltage and temperature; it is measured from 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz with a 0.07 Hz high-pass, a gain-1000 preamplifier and second-order 0.1 Hz high-pass and 10 Hz low-pass stages, inside a Faraday cage. Broadband noise is measured through a 10 Hz high-pass and gain of 11 into a spectrum analyser. An RC low-pass after the output lowers broadband noise, but a large series resistor hurts the response to load steps.

Put low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic capacitors at VIN and VREF, as close to the part as possible, over a solid ground plane. Keep sensitive analog traces away from digital ones and cross them only at right angles. The SOT-23 footprint also takes a 3-pin SOT-23 REF30xx, REF31xx or REF33xx turned 180°: their IN lands on pin 4, OUT on pin 6 and GND on pin 2.
